newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Armed group seizes Slovak in Russia's Ingushetia.
newsitem.headline: Armed group seizes Slovak in Russia's Ingushetia.

text.p: Gunmen have seized a Slovak citizen in Nazran, capital of Russia's North Caucasus region of Ingushetia which borders separatist Chechnya, an Interior Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

"Four camouflage-clad armed men wearing blue berets entered a textile plant in Nazran and seized Dusan Kolac, who worked as a driver there. They then put him in a car and drove away in an unknown direction," the Moscow-based spokesman said.

Kolac, 48, is the fourth foreigner to be taken hostage in the turbulent North Caucasus this month. Frenchman Christophe Andre working for French aid organisation Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF) was abducted in Nazran during the night of July 1 to July 2 and two Britons working for another aid organisation were kidnapped in Chechnya last week.
The Chechen and Ingush authorities, as well as Russian security bodies, are investigating but there has been no word of whereabouts of the three or of any demands by the kidnappers.

In two other incidents on Thursday, reported by Russian news agencies, two Russian construction workers were abducted near the Chechen capital Grozny and an Ingush man was taken hostage by six masked men in Nazran.

Cases of hostage-taking, mainly for ransom, have become common in the region after the end of almost two years of war between Chechen separatists and troops sent in by Moscow. Until recently, most cases had been in Chechnya.
